Finding myself recently stuck without internet for several hours, I watched Donnie Darko again. I know it is an old movie by now, but I still feel the need to warn you not to read any further if you've never seen Donnie Darko before. I will be spoiling several parts of it here.

If you watched the director's cut, at several points it displays text from the pages from the book The Philosophy of Time Travel which is given to Donnie by the the chemistry teacher. This book turns out to be important in understanding the logic of the film, even if you're one of the people who believes that Donnie is either crazy and hallucinating at times, or is in some kind of purgatory, or is merely dreaming the whole thing. By putting the pages shown from that book into the context of the film, one of the major implications is that Donnie and everyone else are now occupying an alternate (tangent) universe which will collapse in a little over 28 days. This tangent universe is essentially a copy of the original, the original being referred to as the "primary universe".

Something that's been bothering me is where the jet engine originally came from at the beginning, so that's the first thing I started to try to figure out. The problem is this: why does the tangent universe contain an extra copy of a single jet engine with no apparent explanation? Why does that extra copy fall from the sky, also with no apparent explanation? "Ah!" You might say, "Donnie sent that engine back in time at the end of the movie!". But you're only half right. Donnie sends the jet engine back in time to the primary universe, remember? When it falls on his room in the beginning of the movie, he's already in the tangent universe. When it falls on him at the end of the movie, he's back in the primary universe. How do we know this? We know this because of Frank, who telepathically calls Donnie away from the house before the engine falls on it. Frank is only granted his powers in the tangent universe in order to direct Donnie to do what he needs to do to save the primary universe.

It turns out most people seem to also be unclear about this, some saying that the appearance of the extra jet engine in the tangent universe is forever a mystery without any way of explaining, while some are even offering explanations which I now think are simply wrong. For example, I came across several explanations in which people think this jet engine is actually the result of a duplication error in the creation of the tangent universe, resulting in 2 copies of the same object simultaneously existing within it, and that this is why the tangent universe is unstable in the first place. But it's important to again note that when the jet engine falls on Donnie at the end of the movie, he's back in the primary universe. That means that the primary universe now also has 2 copies of the same engine. The primary universe is not going to collapse just for that reason. Donnie saved that universe. That was the whole point of all his actions in the tangent universe: to save the primary universe from being destroyed when the tangent universe inevitably collapses. So again, where did the extra engine in the tangent universe come from?

The answer is that the extra jet engine in the tangent universe came from both the primary universe and the tangent universe itself. And yes, Donnie did cause it. Donnie ripped the engine from the plane in the tangent universe and sent it back in time to the primary universe. When the tangent universe is created, since it is a duplicate of the primary universe, it also contains a copy of the engine Donnie sent back in time to the primary universe. Mystery solved. 👍 It may seem simple, but it's not at all obvious from watching the movie, I assure you!

Anarchy and law are, quite simply, the same - which is why you always have National Lawyers' Guild and human rights anarchists side by side, for example. AAA Study: Legal Cannabis Limits are Nonsense but Fatal Crashes Real Threat

They are repeating a well-debunked and deliberate lie.

"Fatal crashes involving drivers who recently used marijuana" implies, incorrectly, that the marijuana played some role in the crash. Even if marijuana usage had zero effect on the likelihood of a crash, you would still expect to see a greater number of marijuana users involved in crashes after a greater number of people are provided access to it.

It's like pointing out that we're seeing a greater number of people having strokes who have recently used marijuana. Well, of course you are. If you randomly test people on the street you'll find a greater number of marijuana users there, too.

This is not to say that it's safe to get I-can't-find-my-lighter stoned and then hop in the car - driving while impaired by anything, including prescription pain meds, will increase risk. But implying causality with this smear - "fatal crashes are a real threat" - is deceptive and unnecessary.

I've seen people get into minor car accidents while stoned and fortunately nothing super damaging, but I'm willing to bet its a bigger problem than we'd like to be comfortable talking about

Oh I agree - I think driving stoned is stupid, and too many people think it's just fine. My argument was against the use of that shitty statistic that keeps getting repeated whenever the topic comes up. Fixing things right means taking about the truth.

I've seen some evidence that there's been a net decrease in car accidents in states where recreational weed is legal. The likely cause of this is the displacement of alcohol use. Driving sober is safest, driving stoned is risky, but driving drunk is even worse. The decrease is nice, but of course not driving impaired at all would be best.

Absent a working field test to measure intoxication, all we have left is the ability to measure impairment itself - can you walk a straight line, count backwards from 100, stuff like that. These tests are tricky too, and it raises the question of why we don't apply them equally to overtired drivers, elderly drivers, and so on. There's not an easy answer there.

We might get lucky and find some clever way to measure impairment that is actually valid and fair. That would solve the problem nicely.
